6. Tuberculinum baby as the very name indicates, has tubercular diathesis; is physically very weak.
There is emaciation of the whole body. Emaciation is very rapid and highly pronounced; losing
flesh while living well. The baby catches cold very easily without knowing how and from
where. The baby usually has family history of tubercular affection. It suits when the best selected
remedies fail to relieve or permanently improve.
7. Sulphur baby is hot and psoric, having scrofulous diathesis; is emaciated and pot bellied. The
baby has dirty and filthy look, weak, tall and stoop shouldered; with all the orifices of the body red.
The baby does not like to be washed or bathed. Cannot bear to stand.
These type of babies may suffer from morning diarrhoea which is painless and involunary and acrid,
causing redness of the anal orifice.
The baby may have skin affections with itch, soreness and boils which come in crops or a single boil

PARTICULARS
Respiratory symptoms : Acalypha Indica is employed in the beginning of phthisis associated with
hard, dry and severe cough followed by bloody expectoration. Expectoration of pure bright red
blood comes on in morning and dark clotted blood in the evening. Cough most violent at night. There is

evening rise of temperature. It is indicated in incipient phthisis with hard, racking cough, bloody
expectoration, arterial haemorrhage but no febrile disturbance.
Gastrointestinal symptoms : This medicine also has marked action on the alimentary canal
characterised by burning in intestines, sensation of weight in stomach, flatulence and spluttering
diarrhoea with forcible expulsion of noisy flatus. (Calc. Phos.) Rectal haemorrhage worse in the
morning.
N.B. Author has releived hundreds of cases of haemoptysis when there is active, bright red bleeding
from the respiratory passages (From bladder : Erigeron, haemorrhage from piles-Mill.)

INTRODUCTION
There are several remedies derived, proved : ‘
and established from Aconite family, the most ; ,
important of which is Aconitum Napellus. Aconite $ si
is one of the deadliest and most rapidly acting ae
poison; yet, through Hahnemann’s discoveries, it *
has been transformed into one of the best of the ay
nurseries. It is one of Clarke’s A, B, C, Nurseries, <
others being Belladonna and Chamomilla. y
Aconite causes Turmoil in circulation,
belladonna causes Turmoil in brain and
Chamomilla causes Turmoil in temperament.
Had it not been for the wonderful curative power —
which Master Hahnemann found and developed fis |
from this wild poisonous plant, we would have
been lagging behind and missed a lot in the
effective treatment of many acute diseases in
their initial stage. Aconite is a short and’quick
acting superficial remedy for acute and most
distressing conditions. Aconite is like a great storm; it comes Suddenly and violently,
sweeps over and passes away in the same manner. With the action of the remedy, the
storm is over. And in this powerful drug, we find a ready solution to many of our staring
problems encountered when dealing with many diseases, provided they are in the initial
stage and the symptoms corroborate.

In the initial stage of any acute diseases such as Apoplexy, Asthma, Chest affection,
Chicken-pox, Cholera, Convulsion, Epilepsy, Croup., Cough, Diarrhoea, Dropsy.
Dysentery, Amenorrhoea, Dysmenorrhoea, Bad effects of fear & fright, Fever, Headache,
Heart affections, Inflammation, Menses, Pneumonia, Suppression of urine, Vertigo, etc.

full:
Thirst during fever : Especially during the heat state, the patient is very much thirsty. There is
burning thirst for large quantity of cold water.
Mental symptoms during fever : The patient is very much anxious. There is intense
nervousness and restlessness, He tosses about in agony. The face is expressive of fear, fear of
death and even predicts the time of death.
Becomes intolerable towards the evening and on going to bed, The patient thinks that he will
definitely die soon and the fever is so severe that it will be fatal to him unless treated immediately.
Modalities :
* Aggravation : Towards the evening and at night and in a warm room.
* Amelioration ; In open air and by prespiration.
General Modalities :
Aggravation : Evening and at night, pains are unsuportable; in a warm room; when rising from
bed; lying on painful or affected side.
Amelioration : In open air.
Relations :
Aconite is complementary to Coffea in fever, sleeplessness and intolerance of pain; to Amica in
traumatism; to Sulphur in all cases, Rarely indicated in fevers which bring out eruptions.
Aconite is the acute of Sulphur and both precede and follow in acute inflammatory conditions.
In Aphonia, when Acon., Phos., Spongia fail, Cina should be thought of.
Antidotes : Bell., Cham., Coffea, Nux v., Sepia, Spongia, Sulph.
Antidoted by: Acet. acid., Alcohol.

2) Sensation of fullness in various parts such as heart, lungs, stomach, anus, brain,

Baby : Baryta carb. baby looks dwarfish in size, with stunted growth; fatty with swollen abdomen
and puffed face. The baby is very chilly and always feels cold to touch and also catches cold very readily.
The baby is highly psoric with tubercular and scrofulous diathesis, (Medorrhinum baby has similar
appearance, but is hot and has sycotic background. Similarly, syphilinum baby too is dwarfish, emaciated,
mentally weak, but chilly and has syphilitic background.) The baby is very much deficient mentally,
idiotic. Child cannot be taught anything or is unable to leam, because he cannot remember. Even the
baby cannot learn the art of walking and consequently, there is late learning to walk (Calc. carb.,
Causicum, Silicea, Calc. phos.).
The baby does not want to play, sits in a comer of the room or street either doing nothing or doing
foolish things such as throwing stones at strangers. The baby becomes serious at laughable matters and
laughs at a serious matter. Saliva runs out from the mouth, both when awake and during sleep’ with
intolerable stench coming from the mouth.
Such children usually has all the glands of the body enlarged, especially enlarged and inflamed tonsils.
caused by Suppressed food sweat. Consequently, tonsillitis is a constant trouble, asscciated with chronic
cold and cough. Every cold settles in throat. Tonsils have the tendency to suppurate and quinsy. Digestion
of the baby is also weak and therefore, he often suffers from diarrhoea, constipation, vomiting etc.

Its action on urinary organs, results in irritation and subsequent inflammation and
formation of renal stone; it produces gall-stone colic. It also has marked action on the
liver promoting the flow of bile or when there is stasis of bile, producing gall-stone.
Therefore, it is an excellent medicine for jaundice and gall-stone.

Physical make-up: Berberis vulgaris is especially suited to those people who are pale.
having earthy complexion with sunken cheeks, having blue rings around eyes.
GUIDING SYMPTOMS P. ae COM oN
1. Left side is principally affected, left kidney and left ureter, » iene
2, Bruised pain with numbness, stiffness in kidney region and in small of back.
3. Soreness of the kidney, bubbling sensation, worse from jar and motion.
4. Backache, worse when sitting or lying, especially when lying on bed in morning.
5. Sensation of numbness, stiffness and lameness with painful pressure in lumbar and
renal region. :
6. Wandering, radiating pains from one part to another, especially along the course of —
left kidney and ureter.

9. Gall-stone colic followed by jaundice.
10. All the symptoms are worse from motion, jar and touch.
11. Urine is greenish, bloody, turbid/and full of slimy mucus.

PARTICULARS
Gall-stone colic :
It has got marked action on the liver and produces various kinds of manifestations.
* Character of pain: There is short, sudden, stabbing, puncturing type of pain in the liver region.
The pain is shooting, tearing, burning, stitching and tingling, wandering from one side to another.
* Modality: Pain is aggravated from little jar and motion,
* Concomitants; Gall stone colic is often associated with jaundice. Stool white, bileless, clay
coloured, o—— =
Urinary Symptoms :
Urine : Constant urging to urinate; sensation as if some urine remained after urinating, with burning
pain in the bladder. The bladder becomes very irritable and urine very slow to flow.
Character of urine: Greenish, bloody with mucus and jelly like sediment. It may be dark, turbid,
with copious sedimentation.
Renal-colic :
* Causation: Due to stone in kidney.
¢ Location: Left sided, starting from left kidney to ureter, then to urinary bladder and coming
down to urethra.
* Sensation:
(1) Numbness in the kidney region.
(2) Bubbling sensation in the kidney region.
(3) Stiffness in the kidnty region.
(4) Lameness and painful pressure in kidney region
(5) Burning and soreness in the kidney region,
© Character of pain; Stitching cutting pains from left kidney following the course of ureter,
bladder and then to urethra. Pain run up to the kidney, burning, stitching in several successive waves in
the region of kidney.
In acute condition, the pain is more severe. There may be haematuria with soreness in urethra.
The character of urine may be bloody, greenish with thick slimy mucus and Jelly-like sediment.
In thronic condition the urine may be dark, turbid with copious sedimentation. Urine is very slow to
flow with constant urging.

name: Respiratory Symptoms
author: Dubey
full:
Coryza : Coryza with corrosive soreness of nose. There is pressure at the root of nose with stoppage
of right nostril. Fan like motion of alae-nasi (Ant tart, Lyco, phos) Sneezing from inhaling dust.
Hoarseness with dry cough & rawness in throat. Hoarseness coming on, from becoming overheated.
Diptheria : In diptheria the formation of diptheric membrane starts in bronchi, trachea or larynx and
extending upwards. Chest pain runs upwards. There is membranous and dipth-eritic croup with much
rattling during cough but no choking.
Cough : During whooping cough there is croupy symptoms with hoarseness. Patient gasps for
breath. Cough, spasmodic with rattling of mucus. Every inspiration provokes cough. Cold sensation in
larynx is characteristic.
Asthma : It is a very good medicine for sailors’ asthma. Sailors suffer from asthma “on shore”
or when they come on land & better at sea. .
Dyspnoea : With inability to inspire deep cough. There is sensation as if breathing through a sponge
or the air passages are full of smoke or vapour of sulphur.
Sexual Symptoms :
Male : Swelling & induration of testicles with pains worse slight jar.
Female ; Menses : Too early ; too profuse with membranous shreds. Low spirited before menses.
Breast: Tumour in breasts with stitching pains, worse left. Stitch-pains from breasts to axillae: Sharp
shooting pain in left breast, worse pressure.
General Modalities :
Aggravation : From evening, until midnight. when sitting in warm room, warm, damp weather.,
Amelioration : From any motion, exercise, at sea.
Relations : Compare : in croup & croupy affections, chlor. Hep., lod, Spong. Bromium had cured
croup after failure of lod., Phos., Spong., Hep.,
Hard goitre was cured after lod. failed.
N.B. : “The Chief distinction between Brom. and lod. Is, the former cures the blue-eyed and the
latter the black-eyed patients”"—Hering.

1. Camphor is the UNIVERSAL ANTIDOTE TO THE MEDICINES PREPARED
FROM VEGETABLE KINGDOM.
2. The patient is exceedingly sensitive to cold air (Hepar. sulph., Nux vom., Kali carb.
and Rumex).
8. Surface cold to touch, chilliness, yet cannot bear to be covered, throws off
all the coverings (Secale cor., Med., wants covering,—Hepar, Psor., Nux Vom. and
Rumex),
4. Collapsed condition with coldness and lividity are the leading features of
Camphor.
5. Pain is better while thinking of it. (Hell.), (Worse, Calc. phos.. Baryta carb., Medo.
and Gels.)
6. Profound prostration with rapid sinking of strength. ‘
7. Scantiness of discharges: e.g. diarrhoea, vomiting, sweat, urine, etc. is characteristic
to Camphor and Camphor only.
8. Entire body painfully sensitive to slight touch (Kali carb. and Spigelia).
9. Camphor has internal heat and external coldness.
10. Cramps with icy coldness of limbs is a characteristic of Camphor.
11. Repercussed eruption of measles and scarlatina. In all sequelae of measles.
12. Camphor is indicated in many conditions of sudden collapse from over powering
influence.
13. Bad effects of shock from injury, eruptions suppressed, cold air, sunstroke and
vexation.
14. Mind : Mentally there is great anxiety and extreme fear, fear of persons, of strange
atmospheres, of darkness. The patient goes into a state of imbecility. The
appearence is, as if it had come on slowly. There is delirious condition, with heat,
rage and mania; anxiety, tosses about anxiously in bed with almost loss of
conciousness,
PARTICULARS
Cholera :
It typifies the collapse stage of Asiatic Cholera, says Dr. N.M. Chowdhury.
* Stage: In the first stage of Cholera morbus and Aslatic Cholera,
* Onset: Sudden attack of vomiting and diarrhoea.
* Quantity; There is not much discharge from the bowels, not much vomiting, sweat and urine,
but suddenly the patient CoLLAPsEs..
Great coldness of surface, body cold to touch yet cannot bear to be covered. Throws off
all the coverings. With collapse, there is great prostration and rapid sinking of strength.
ee |
Character of discharge: Stool rice-watery, involuntary, blackish, dark brown, faeces like coffee- |
ground, SCANTY with great tenesmus.
There is great retching and straining to vomit with SCANTY DISCHARGE. |
Cramps: There are cramps in .the stomach and bowels spreading to other parts of the body,
especially in calf muscles.
Look of the face: The face is cold, blue and shrivelled, very much anxious and pale.
Sweat; There is scanty sweat which is cold, all over the body, but more on the forehead, (Ver, alb.),
Tongue: The tongue is cold, flabby and trembling with cold breath
Pulse: Weak, small, slow, scarcely perceptible.
It differs in cholera from Cuprum and Veratrum album.
In Camphor, there is great PROSTRATION, BLUENESS, COLDNESS of the body and the body is
cold and dry, yet the patient wants to be uncovered. And all the discharges are SCANTY.
in Cuprum, there is not so much prostration and coldness but there is more cramping and more
convulsive tendency. So, the more the cramping the better the Cuprum is indicated,
In Ver. Alb., the more copius the discharge from bowels and the more profuse the vomiting and
sweat.
So scanty, cold and dry is Camphor; cold and copiousn discharge is Ver.alb.
The collapse of Camphor is sudden and overwhelming but not so in Ver. alb., due to excess of
Fever :
In eruptive fever, especially in measles, the face is pale, blue, cold and hippocratic face. The body is
cold to touch, still the patient likes to he uncovered.
When eurptions do not appear or in repercussed eruption of measles and scarlatina, in all Sequelae
of measles, Camphor is a great remedy.
General Modalities :
Aggravation: By motion, at night and in cold air.
Amelioration : When thinking of exsiting complaints and warm air,
Relations :
Camphor antidotes nearly every vegetable medicine, tobacco, and opium.
Compare: Veratrum, Secale and Cuprum in cholera.
Antidoted by: Dulc., Phos. and Op.

name: Physiological Action
author: Dubey
full:
It has at least three special centres of action through the nervous system.
1) Liver—It acts upon the liver and portal system giving rise to jaundice and bilious
disturbances.
2) Bowels—Here it acts as a laxative producing a catarrhal discharge.
3) Kidneys—It produces diuresis.

exhaustion and it inhibits enzyme action, thus retarding tissue metabolism. It also

varying types, especially intermittent type.

loss of vital fluids and abuse of quinine.

become weak, debilitated and exhausted by loss of vital fluids such as haemorrhage,
diarrhoea, suppuration, lactation, etc.

Relation with heat and cold: Chilly patient.

name: Physiological Action
author: Dubey
full:
It has seven special centres of action through the cerebrospinal nervous system.
1) Cerebrum : Here it stimulates the mentality and produces obstinate insomnia.
2) Cord, posterior columns : It paralyzes the sensory nerve filaments.
3) Circulation : It stimulates the vasomotor nerves and increases blood pressure.
4) Kidneys : Here it increases the arterial blood pressure, produces diuresis and
diminishes the urea.
5) Sexual organs : Producing great excitement of these organs which is followed by
paresis.
6) Digestive organs : It first stimulates the digestive organs and then prostrates
them.
7) Vagi: It very powerfully stimulates the respiratory centre,
CONSTITUTION

Temperament: Sanguine choleric temperament.

PARTICULARS
Headache : ‘
Causation: Anger with indignation and mortification, vexation, taking cheese, suppressed menses
and exposure to cold.
Location: Headache is normally felt in the frontal region. .
Character of pain: There is pressive and burning pain in the frontal region with soreness of scalp.
Modalities: Headache is worse by stooping, lying on back, anger and indignation. Better by pressure
and by bending head forward.
Concomitants: Confusion and pressive pain in orbit; vertigo on quickly turning the head.
Vertigo :
Causation: Anger, indignation, mortification, vexation, suppressed menses and exposure to cold.
Character: There is VERTIGO ON QUICKLY TURNING the HEAD, especially to the left, as if he
would fall, with confusion and pressive pain in the orbit. Dullness and giddiness at the beginning of colic.
accompained by pressive frontal headache.
Colic :
Causation: Anger with indignation, vexation, taking cheese, exposure to cold and suppressed
Menses.
Location: Colicky Pain is felt in the whole abdomen. ;
Character of pain: There is terrible agonising pain in the abdomen, compelling the patient
to bend double, pain is violent and gripping type. Abdomen is very sensitive to touch. Pains come in
paroxysms; become very severe every few minutes. The patient twists and turns to get relief.
Modalities: .
* Aggravation by eating and drinking, by taking cheese, and by touch.
* Amelioration: By bending double, motion, bending forward, hard pressure and discharge of
flatus.
Concomitants: Colicky pain may be attended with neuralgia; headache of violent nature with cutting
and boring pain in the head.

Modality: Relief by pressure and lying on affected side.

* Concomitants: Headache is associated with gouty affection.
Intermittent fever :
Eupatorium perfoliatum is adapted to various types of intermittent fever e.g., tertian, double tertian,
postponing and bilious fever.
Time: The time of paroxysms is generally between 7 and 9 a.m. Postponing type. i.e., one day at
7 a.m. the next day at 9 a.m. and then at 11 a.m. and so on.
Before the attack: There may be nausea and vomiting and sometimes there are spells of vomiting
of bile. There is great thirst for several hours before the fever.
During the attack: There is extremely severe chill. Shivering runs down the back and spreads from
the back to the extremities. There is SORENESS and pulsation in the back of the head. Violent pain in
the occiput and back before and during chill.
During the chill, the patient wants to cover up the whole body. There is bitter vomiting at the close
of chill.
There is bruised feeling as if broken all over the body, bone pain affecting back, chest, limbs,
especially the wrists which feel as if dislocated. The more general and severe the pain, the better it is
indicated and adapted.
There is insatiable thirst before and during chill and fever. The patient knows that chill is
coming because he cannot drink enough. He has violent thirst but the shivering becomes worse from
drinking. So he dares not drink cold water. With- fever there is bursting type of headache. There is sweat
which relieves all the symptoms except headache.
Bryonia is its nearest analogue having free sweat but there, pain keeps the patient quiet while
Eupatorium has scanty sweat and pains make the patient restless.
General Modalities :
Aggravation: Periodically and in open air.
Amelioration: Conversation, by getting on hands and knees, sweat (except in headache).

the R.B.C. count causing FALSE PLETHORA but later on it produces anaemia. A

congestion, increased blood pressure and haemorrhage. In alimentary canal, peristalsis
is weakened, producing vomiting, constipation, diarrhoea, etc.

chlorotic, yet have a FIERY RED FACE.
Temperament: Sanguine temperament easily vexed, least contradiction excites the
patient.
Relation with heat and cold: Hot patient.

Headache :
Causation: Loss of vital fluid, abuse of quinine and suppressed intermittents.
Time: Periodic type of headache, every 2,3 or 4 days or every 2 or 3 weeks.
Character of pain: Hammering, beating, pulsating type of pain in head, Congestive type of
headache, pain in the back of head. Pain compels the patient to lie down:
Modalities: Aggravation by coughing and amelioration by pressure and Slow walking about.
Concomitants: With headache, there is vertigo with balancing sensation as if on water; also there
may be aversion to eating and drinking.
Vertigo :
When there is vertigo, the patient feels a peculiar sensation of balancing, as if on water, or the vertigo
appears on seeing flowing water, or as if walking over water when crossing a bridge, or on descending.

Time: At night (China, Puls., Chel).
Character: Painless, with ineffectual urging; stool contains undigested food particles.
Modality: Aggravation at night, WHILE EATING AND DRINKING.
Concomitants: With diarrhoea, there is good appetite and prolapse of rectum. The diarrhoea causes
progressive emaciation of the patient.
Constipation :
Cause: From intestinal atony.
Character of stool: Stool is dry, knotty, with ineffectual urging. Stool is followed by backache and
cramping pain in the rectum; prolapse of rectum and itching of anus at night.
Concomitants: Along with hard, dry, knotty, stool, there is prolapse of rectum and itching of anus.
Menses :
Time: Too early.
Quantity: Too profuse.
Duration: Too long lasting.
Character of blood: Bright red, easily coagulable. Discharge of long pieces of membrane from

Concomitants: With menses, there is ringing in the ears.

Modality: Cough is relieved by lying down and eating.

Remittent fever :
Causation: Due to heat of sun, warmth or cold.
Onset: Insidious, slow and gradual.
During fever: There are DULLNESS, DIZZINESS, AND DROWSINESS accompanied with languor,
muscular weakness and desire for absolute rest. Great heaviness of head and limbs.
The tongue is trembling with complete absence of thirst.
There is severe headache which is relieved by profuse urination. The pulse is full and flowing.
Stuporous conditions may appear in late stage.
After fever: There may be paralysis of various group of muscles.
Gels, has also proved prophylactic against Influenza.
Paralysis :
Gelsemium is a great paralyser.
Character: The onset of the paralysis is gradual, It produces a general state of paresis, mental and
physical. “TREMOR” is the key-note of the remedy, While the mind is absolutely sluggish, the whole
body, particularly the muscular system, is relaxed. The limbs are so HEAVY and painful that the patient
can hardly move them. There is complete relaxation and prostration of the whole muscular system
with entire motor paralysis. Weakness and trembling of tongue, hands, legs and entire body. LACK
OF MUSCULAR COORDDNATION IS WELL MARKED; CONFUSED; MUSCLES REFUSE TO OBEY
THE WILL. Locomotor ataxia and paraplegia are successfully treated by this great remedy.
The same paretic coridition is present in eyelids, causing ptosis and diplopia; in oesophagus,

name: Pathogenesis
author: Dubey
full:
Its action on skin produces degenerative changes, manifestation of various kinds of
skin eruptions from which oozes a WATERY, TRANSPARENT AND STICKY FLUID. It
exerts a general influence on nutrition of skin; whereby it causes diarrhoea, chronic
constipation ete. in the digestive system and excessive menstrual ailment, leucorrhoea,
ete. in sexual organs.
CONSTITUTION
Make-up of the body: Usually a lady of climacteric age, fair, fat and flabby, having
irregular deposition of fat at selected locations of the body, waxy and anaemic face, split
hair, unhealthy skin, brittle and deformed nails, suffering from habitual constipation and
with a history of delayed rnenstruation,
Temperament: Irritable and melancholic.
Relation with heat and cold; Very chilly patient.
a
Miasm: Psora is in the background.
Diathesis: Tubercular and cancerous diathesis.
GUIDING SYMPTOMS .
1. Especially adapted to woman of climacteric age, generally inclined to obesity, who
suffers from habitual constipation and with history of delayed menstruation.
2. A marked characteristic of Graphites is rush of blood to head with flushed face
or rush of blood to head with distention and flatulence.
3. Cracks and fissures on end of fingers and toes, nipples, labial commissures, anus,
etc. 4 Anie om”
4. From the moist skin eruptions oozes a watery, transparent and sticky
fluid. Whenever such eruptions are found Graph, is in all probability the remedy.
5. Disposition to delayed menstruation.
6. Gastralgia better by eating or by drinking hot milk.
7. Sexual debility from sexual abuse; and decided aversion to coition.
8. Hears better in noise and when riding in a carriage.
9. Music makes her weep. She thinks of nothing but death.
10. Desire for hot milk which relieves constipation and gasf¥ic; complaints. AVERSION
to meat, fish, salt, cooked food and sweets.
11. Mind : Ailments from grief and vexation.
There is great dread of mental and physical work, with, excessive depression of
mind. Patient is very sad; thinks of nothing but death and salvation. But there is
changeable mood. The patient can remember past events, but forgets the recent
occurrences.
Sensation of a cobweb over fa head; tries hard to brush it off. MUSIC
MAKES WEEP and also increases her sufferings. The patient is excessively
cautious, timid, hesitating and unable to decide about anything. She is always sad
and despondent.
12. Ailments from : Grief and vexation; suppression of skin eruptions; extremes of heat
and cold; overlifting. _
PARTICULARS
Headache :
Causation: From grief, vexation, extremes of heat and cold.
Location: Congestive pain especially in the occiput; extends to the nape of neck, stitching pain in
temples.
Character of headache: Pain as though the head were numb, violent headache as if the Head would
burst, congestive, constriqtive and stitching pain.
Modality: Aggravation at night and during menstruation and relieved by lying down, fs
Concomitants: Vertigo as if intoxicated. Nausea, vomiting and eructation especially during menses,
along with headache, itching of scalp; burning on vertex.
Ears :
Hears better when in a noise, when riding in a carriage or when there is a rumbling sound
(Nitric.acid), Loss of hearing with dryness of ears; cracking, humming and roaring in ears. Swelling of the
glands under the ear.
Castro-intestinal tract :
Mouth : Sour, salty, bitter or putrid taste in the mouth like rotten eggs, with frequent eructations
tasting of ingesta. Foul odour from mouth; increased salivation with much spitting.
Stomach : There is nausea and vomiting especially in the morning; griping colic with constrictive
pain below umbilicus. Periodic gastralgia with vomiting of entire food immediately after eating. Chronic
catarrh in the stomach with frequent eructation. Pain is relieved by drinking hot milk.
Diarrhoea : The patient gives a definite history of habitual constipation but suffers occasionally from
diarrhoea too.
* Causation: Diarrhoea from suppressed skin eruption and alcohol (Petroleum).
* Character of stool: Stool is brown, fluid mixed with undigested substances of an
intolerable foetid odour. The diarrhoea is usually painless.
* Concomitants: Associated with purging, vomiting and ice cold sweat.
Constipation : Graphites patient is generally constipated. The stool is very hard, in large lumps,
difficult to evacuate, knotty; lumps are united together with mucous threads.
There may be dryness of mucous membrane of rectum, with fissure of anus. There is sharp, smarting
and sore pain in anus after stool. Haemorrhoid protrudes while passing stool, associated with burning
pain, cracks and fissure.
Modality: Constipation is relieved by drinking hot milk (Rhus tox.—lodum, by cold milk).
Menses : é-'
Time: Delayed from getting feet wet.
Quantity: Too scanty.
Duration: Short.
Character of blood; Too pale.
Concomitants: There is violent colicky pain during menses. There may also be morning sickness at
the time of menstruation. The patient is weak and prostrated. Leucorrhoea before or after menses in
FAT, CHILLY and. CONSTIPATED ladies. Swelling and pain in right ovarian region before and during
menses.
Leucorrhoea :
In a Graphites patient, leucorrhoea appears before and after menses and it is very much acrid, and
excoriating; OCCURS IN GUSHES DAY AND NIGHT.
Skin:
Graphites is a great remedy for all sorts of skin eruptions with a tendency towards malignancy e.g.
keloid, fibroma, pimples, acne, eczema, cancer of the breast, hard and painful cicatrices which have got
eS
a tendency to break open again. Erysipelas beginning in the face and spreading to other parts. Every little
injury suppurates. Fissures and cracks at the end of fingers, or nipples, vulva and labial commissures.
There is itching of skin over the body with or without eruptions. Skin affections are particularly
located in the bend of joints, on the scalp and behind the ears.
All the skin eruptions have one thing in common, viz. they EXUDE A WATERY, TRANSPARENT,
GELATINOUS. STICKY FLUID. Hard cicatrices appearing after mammary abscess, retarding the flow of
milk. Old cicatrices break open again. Cancer of breast, from old scars and repeated abscesses. Eruptions
upon the ears; between the fingers and toes and on various parts of body from which oozes a
WATERY, TRANSPARENT AND STICKY FLUID.
The nails are brittle, crumbling, and deformed; they are very painful and sore as if ulcerated, thick
and crippled. Eczema of lids, eruptions moist and fissured, lids red and margins covered with scales and
crusts. There is burning in round spot on vertex. Phlegmonous erysipelas on face with burning pain,
commences on right side, going to left, after application of iodine.
Skin affections are not inclined to heal, but ulcerate readily, with itching over various parts of the
body, followed by burhing and oozing with typical STICKY FLUID discharge. Suppression of skin
eruptions causes diarrhoea (Petroleum).
Clarke says, “The skin of Graphites is rough, hard and dry” Eczematous and herpetic eruptions
predominate. Eruption on occiput exuding gluey humour; eczema of ears; moist eczema round anus.
Pimples, acne, gastro-intestinal affections alternating with acne and erythema of face, herpetic lesions or
scrofulous hypochondriasis. Excoriation between toes. Syphilitic and constitutional ulcers. Recrudescence
of scars, cracks and fissures. Offensive discharges and secretions. Sweat stains garments yellow with sour
and offensive smell.
Modalities: Skin affections are aggravated at night, by warmth of bed, before and during
menstruation and during change of weather. Amelioration is from open air, wrapping up and in darkness.
General Modalities :
Aggravation: Warmth in general, at night, rich food, before and after menstruation, extremes of
temperature, draught of cold, air, uncovering and cold drinks. =
Amelioration: From warm drink, particularly warm milk, from being wrapped up, open air,
eructation and eating.
Relations :
Complementary to: Causticum, Hepar and Lycopodium.
Antidoted by: Aeon., Nux vom.
Antidotes: Are., lod., Rhus tox.

After Sulphur in affections of skin.
For obesity in young women after Calcarea carb.

Eye:

Ticking cough with taste of blood or sulphur; without effort or coughing; sometimes lasts for months

Throbbing pain in stomach. PROFUSE BLEEDING DARK BLOOD, SORENESS IN THE

Dark blood with increased desire to urinate.

Rheumatism : Sore bruised feeling. When Arnica fails, think of Hamamelis.

* During cough: The patient goes on coughing and sweating. He coughs and sweats. There is
much sweating without any relief.
* Modalities: Cough is worse in the moming, from exposure to dry west wind, cold air, cold
drinks, before mid-night and towards evening.
* Amelioration by warmth and in damp wet weather.
Asthma :
* Causation: After suppression of skin eruption.
* Character: Breathing difficult, with rattling and wheezing sound in the chest. The patient has to
take deep breath with threatened suffocation.
* Modality: The patient must bend head backwards and sit up which gives him temporary relief.
Better in DAMP wet weather and by covering the body.
Skin :
Hepar sulph. is a great remedy for skin affection; whatever may be the name of the disease, such as
eczema, itch, herpes, psoriasis, urticaria, acne, boils, abscess, rash, eruptions of all catogories. It has
unhealthy suppurating skin. EVERY LITTLE INJURY SUPPURATES (Sulphur, Graphites, Silicea). The
skin is very much sensitive and sore to touch. The skin and eruptions are so sensitive that the
patient cannot bear even the touch of the cloth. Eczema spreads by means of new pimples appearing just
above the old ones. Boils, abscesses and papules are prone to suppuration. Ulcers are very sensitive to
contact, easily bleeding, burning and stinging. Cannot bear to be uncovered; wants to be wrapped up
warmly.
In ABSCESSES AND BOILS where suppuration is inevitable, Hepar, if given in high potency, aborts
the abscess and in low potency it hastens suppuration and heals quickly.
Hepar Sulph. is prepared by mixing Calcarea carb, and Sulphur. Its symptoms, however, show wide

Between the two great suppurative medicines viz., Hepar and Silica.

in it, want of self-confidence, lack of “grit”, timidity, sufferings from anticipation as when having to appear

even subject to sudden murderous impulses.

name: Gastro-Intestinal Symptoms
author: Dubey
full:
Mouth : Blisters on lips. A coated large flabby yellow tongue. Tongue feels burnt. Swollen and easily
bleeding gums. Toothache unbearable when food touches the teeth.
Stomach : Appetite poor, bad taste in mouth. Eructations like rotten eggs. Continued rising-of white
froth into mouth. Cannot digest milk, it causes pain in stomach and passes undigested. Complaints
aggravated from salty food & sea bathing,
Liver: Chronic liver complaints with tenderness and pressing pain extending to-spine and
epigastrium. Enlarged, sore mvt with flatulence.
Aggravation : Lying on right side, after food.
Amelioration ; By hard pressure.
Constipation : It is mostly indicated in obstinate constipation and of infants during dentition. The
characteristic stool is hard, knotty, scanty, passes with difficulty with crumbling at verge of anus. After
stools rectum feels sore & painful. Constipation at sea (Bry., Platina.)
Menses : The flow is black and clotted. Profuse at night, in bed causing hysterical symptoms. The
Menstrual pain is generally relieved by having back pressed. There is great excitement at every period,
and pains in the back while walking and in the thighs when sitting. Eruptions on face and forehead worse
before menses.
Leucorrhoea : After exertion, after every stool, or following uterine spasm. It may be followed by
Metrorrhagia. Leucorrhoea two weeks after menses for three or four days.
General modalities :
Aggravation—Lying on right side, sea bathing, immediately after eating.
Amelioration—From pressure, motion, open air (except headache).
Relations :
Antidotes : Cham. Camph.
Compare : Chamomilla in diseases of children.

Menses :
First menstruation at puberty delayed.
Time: Too early.
Duration: Irregular mense which may be of various types i.e., too early or too late, too scanty or too
profuse.
Concomitants: Bearing down pain which is worse in the morning. Hot feeling during menses.
Headache after menses, Sterility with too early and too profuse menstruatton.
Anaemia :
Causation: Loss of vital fluid.
It causes alteration in blood and hence produces anaemia: Cachectic condition and chlorotic look.
Blue rings around the eyes and oedema with other generalities of the drug.
Skin :
Eczema :
* Location: Especially on the margins of hair, scalp, behind the ears.
* Look: Raw, red inflamed and ulcerated.
* Modality:
Aggravation : From earing too much salt, at sea shore or from ocean voyage.
Amelioration: \n open air and by cold bathing.
Urticaria : Acute or chronic, over whole body, especially after violent exercise.
Herpes : Herpetic eruptions especially around the edges of hair and nape of neck.
Warts : On palms of hands (Anac., On dorsum of hand, Dulc.).
Fever blisters : Blisters at the sides of mouth in intermittent fever, like-small pearls about the
lips with lips dry, sore, crackedand ulcerated.
Nail : Hangnails, skin around the nails dry and cracked (Graph, Petrol.).
Fever :
Natrum mur., is a medicine which should be thought of especially in chronic intermittent fever. The
symptoms are as follows:-
Causation: Abuse of quinine, old, chronic, badly treated and neglected cases of fever.
Character: Periodicity well marked. Chill returns in the morning, especially at 10 to 11 A.M. Fever
with severe headache, left sided clavus as if a thousand little hammers were knocking in the brain with
coldness of the body and chilliness well marked.
Modality: Sweat on every little exertion with RELIEF OF ALL THE SUFFERINGS.
Concomitants: Fever blisters, especially at the corners of mouth. MAPPED TONGUE with red
insular patches...
Look of the baby: Pale, anaemic, weak and emaciated, emaciation especially marked in the
neck, with long neck (short neck Kali bich,), There is descending type of marasmus. Baby LOSES

cause. The child gets into a passion about trifles, especially when consoled, consolation aggravates all
troubles.
Desire and Aversion: The baby has intense craving for salt and child has great aversion to

Tongue :
The baby is having MAPPED TONGUE. Slow in learning to talk, with heavy and difficult speech.
Stool: Usually constipated.
Urine: There is involuntary urination while coughing, sneezing and laughing.
Modalities:
* Aggravation : From taking excessive salt and heat of sun.
¢ Amelioration: Going without regular meals arid open air.
General Modalities :
Aggravation: From sunrise to sunset, especially from 10 to 11 a.m. At seashore, from sea air heat of
sun, mental exertion, lying down and by consolation,
Amelioration: In the open air, cold bathing, going without regular meals, lying on right side
(Sulphur).
Relations :
Complementary to: Apis.
Natrum mur. is the chronic of Ignatia, but in mental plane only.
Is followed well by: Sepia and Thuja.

name: Pathogenesis
author: Dubey
full:
By its action on the spinal cord, brain, motor and sensory nerve centres, a condition
of EXCESSIVE IRRITATION AND EXCITABILITY is produced which causes muscular
incoordination and paralysis. It acts on the organs and their nutrition, thereby the
secretions are altered, functions are perverted and the organic; substances change. A
long chain of symptoms set in presenting an accurate picture of gastric, hepatic and
intestinal affections. It irritates the mucous membrane of alimentary tract, thereby
producing dyspepsia like symptoms and stimulate constipation, diarrhoa, dysentery, etc.
Affections of the respiratory system result in dry catarrhal condition, obstruction of nose
and cough. It stimulatesthe vasomotoricentre and thus gives rise to blood pressure, heart
symptoms etc.
CONSTITUTION
Make-up of the body: Nux vomica is ideally suited to thin spare subjects, with dark
hair and dark complexion, who lead a sedentary life, nervous, extremely susceptible to
external impressions, habituated to overstudy, debauches, zealous and hypochondriac.
People of all walks of life, from the highest to the lowest standard, richest or poorest,
civilised or unciuilsed.
Temperament: Bilious, sanguine, irritable and impatient temperament.
“Nux is chiefly successful with persons of an ardent character; of an irritable.
impatient temperament, disposed to anger, spite or deception’—says Hahnemann.
Relation with heat and cold: Nux vom. is a very CHILLY remedy.
Miasm: Definitely psora isin the background as the originator of all the troubles.

powers, lessons self control and power of concentration, judgment, stimulates the
imagina-tion. It checks all secretions except that of skin, which is excited.

high family and all others are of lower category.
“Superiority complex” of the highest degree runs through the whole remedy. She
looks down upon others with contemptuous eyes and thinks everyone else is very
much inferior to her.
There is mental delusion as if everyone and everything is inferior to herself. All
persons physically and mentally are smaller than her, and that she is large and
superior to all others She imagines that all about her are second to none and there
is sensation of herself growing larger in every direction
There are HYSTERICAL PATIENTS, who are alternately gay and sad. One moment
excessively happy and the next moment sad and gloomy (Crocus sat., Puls., Ign.,
Nux mos.). Can cry easily any moment. Such ladies are very much arrogant, proud
and naughty.
There is satiety of life with taciturnity and fear of death. Trifling things produce
profound vexation. Anxious and serious over silly matters (Anacardium, Baryta
carb.).
There is fear of death, with loathing of life. Fears that something serious will
happen to her.,
Trembling of all the limbs during even a little exertion,
“Mental symptoms appear as physical symptoms disappear and vice versa” is the
most rare, uncommon and characteristic sympiom of this drug.

name: Pathogenesis
author: Dubey
full:
It produces irritation and catarrhal inflammation of mucous membrane, HAVING
THICK BLAND, GREEN YELLOWISH DISCHARGES, venous engorgement and
congestion. It causes contractive pains in uterus. Pulsatilla also causes burning
sensation on palms and soles and tongue. Furthermore, it produces arthritic or
rheumatic inflammation. The veins seem to lose their vital resistance under the
influence of Pulsatilla so that varicosis occurs, especially of rectum. In eyes it acts on lids
producing inflammation and catarrhal discharge. From the ear too, there is purulent
discharge.
CONSTITUTION
Physical make-up: Usually ladies who are fair and beautiful-looking but inclined to
be fleshy with fine hair and blue eyes, soft and lax muscels, anaemic and chlorbtic with
pale face at puberty. Pulsatilla patient can be compared to the race of SHEEP, as Antim
crud. to SWINE and Arsenic to RACE of HORSE
Temperament: Full of tears, slow, phelgmatic and indecisive.
Relation with heat and cold: It is controversial point whether Pulsatilla is a hot or
chilly drug. Dr. KENT says that there is a pendulum like action between heat and cold
relation amongst complementary remedies.
TYLER BOERICKE AND ALLEN say that it is a chilly drug. KENT says that it is a
hot blooded patient. But after using the remedy for some time, it will be noticed that the
patient goes to the other extreme and becomes chilly or hot as the case may be.
Miasm: Psoric and sycotic miasms are in the background.

PARTICULARS
Headache :
Causation : Headache is from overloading the stomach, fatty diet and stooping.
Location: One sided headache especially in the forehead and temples.
Sensation : One sided headache especially in the forehead.
Character: Bruised pain, stupefying headache. There is great heaviness on stooping. Dullness of
head; headache with aching pain in the eyes. Throbbing, pressive headache, pressive and constrictive
pain in temples; violent pain on one side as if a nail was driven in beating, jerking and lacerating
headache.
Modalities: Aggravation by stooping, lying down or exposure to cold,
Relief by sitting, in the morning and by pressure.
Concomitants: Confusion in head, vertigo as if intoxicated with nausea and inclination to vomit.
Apoplexy with unconsciousness: violent beating in head, pain in the eyeballs.
Eyes :
There is dryness of eyes and lids; with sensation as if darkened by mucous. Pressure as from sand in
eyes. Conjunctivitis with PROFUSE, THICK, YELLOW, BLAND DISCHARGE; BURNING AND
ITCHING in the eyes and inflammation of eyes, margins of eyelids with lachrymation and nightly
agglutination. There may be styes, especially on upper eyelids with itching, biting and burning. Opthalmia
may also be treated successfully with Pulsatilla.
Gastro-intestinal tract :
Mouth : Mouth is dry in the morning without thirst. Bad taste and smell from mouth in the morning.
Accumulation of saliva in the mouth.
Saliva gives sweetish taste; constant spitting of frothy cotton like mucous (Nux mos.).
Tongue : Loss of taste: nothing tastes good. In catarrh, the tongue is white or yellow and coated
with tenacious mucus.
Tongue is parched dry, yet no thirst. Tongue feels too broad and too large; edge of tonque feels
sore as if scalded.
Toothache worse in morning and at night and in a warm room, Pain in gums.
Stomach :
* Causation: Eating rich and fatty food, fruits, ice-cream, tea, worms in case of children; weakness
of stomach, indigestion and suppressed menses.
The above factors may cause nausea, vomiting, epigastric pain, abdominal colic and diarrhoea.
* Nausea: Felt in the throat as if worms are crawling, nausea may end in vomiting.
Vomiting of blood or of bilious matter. Therefore, the vomitus is green with pale face and
chilliness; but not thirst.
* Epigastric pain: There is pain in the pit of stomach, The character of pain and the
accompanying symptoms are just as mentioned above under item No. 4 of the guiding symptoms.
There is sensation of weight as from a stone in the stomah, about an hour after eating. Pressure
in pit of stomach after meals with growing distress when stomach is empty.

Colic : Flatulent colic after supper or at night. Oppressive flatulence in upper abdomen and
hypochondria. Colic and pain obliges the patient to bend forward. Abdomen js painful and sensitive to
touch.
Diarrhoea :
* Causation: Fatty food, fruits, cold drinks, ice-cream, etc.
¢ Time: Only or usually at night (China).
* Character of stool: Watery stool, sometimes unconsciously evacuated. Greenish, yellow and
slimy. NO TWO STOOLS ARE ALIKE, very much changeable.
* Concomitants: Dry tongue with no thirst.
* Modality: Aggravation: At night, by fatty food, ice-cream, tea, etc.
Respiratory symptoms :
Cough :
* Causation: Usually caused by irritation in pit of stomach, by taking ice cold things, fatty and
starchy food, ice-cream, or due to suppressed menses.
* Sensation: Pressure and soreness upon the chest.
* Character of cough: Cough is shaking and spasmodic; in paroxysms of two coughs (Merc.
sol.—3 paroxysms, Cup met., Stannum—Single paroxysm, Calc. Carb.). The patient feels as if vapour of
sulphur is in trachea and chest. Cough is dry, in the evening and at night.
* Character of sputa: Expectoration of COPIOUS AND GREENISH YELLOW MUCUS. Bitter
or purulent or there may be dark coagulated blood.
* Modality: Aggravation: By warmth of bed, night, evening, after every sleep and after lying
down.
* Concomitants; Involuntary urination while coughing there may be pain in lower part of chest,
more severe the pain more severe the chill, anguish and shuddering.
There may also be phthisis in suppurative stage in chlorotic girls. Further more, there may be asthma
in young girls dure to suppressed menses. There may also be stitching pain in chest, worse frotn deep
breath and persistent bronchial catarrh. *
Reproductive System :
Menses : All complaints can be traced to the time of puberty. Ailments on and from the pubertic
age. “Has never.been well since that time”.
Many of the complaints originate from suppressed menses.
* Causation: After getting feet wet.
* Time: Delayed menses comes too late.
* Duration: Shon duration of menses is very well marked.
* Quantity: Scanty menses.
* Character of blood: Flow is thick and changeable in character. Blood flows, stops and flows
again. Sometimes intermittent flow, mixed with clots or water, coagulable in character. Flow is more
during day and while walking.

Leucorrhoea : Milky white, with swollen vulva. Acrid, burning and painless or with cutting pain in
abdomen. While all the discharges are bland, leucorrhoea is acrid, excoriating and corrodes the vulva.
Labour pain : Difficult and irregular, sluggish labour pain. During labour pain the patient wants
doors and windows open. Cannot bear stuffy warm room. Feels suffocated. Dr. Huges praises Pulsatilla
for its spontaneous version in case of abnormal presentation; useful in retained placenta, postpartum
haemorrhage, etc.
Abortion : Threatened abortion, the flow ceases and starts again with double force and ceases
again. Pulsatilla promotes expulsion of moles, says Hering.
General Modalities :
Aggravation: Warm air, warm room, warmth of bed, heat in the evening, lying on the left or on the
painless side, rest, rich and fatty food, puberty, pregnancy when allowing feet to hang down.
Amelioration: Cold, air, erect position, motion, open air after a good cry, lying on painful side, cold
application, cold food and drinks, though not thirsty.

Inimical to: Sepia.
Antidotes: China, Coffea, Ignaria, Nux, Sulphur.
Antidoted by; China, Lyco.
Complementaries: Silica, Fluoric acid, Kali mur., Lyco.

and inflame under the influence of Rhus tox. When circulatory system becomes the seat of its action, it
causes a state of blood poisoning typhoid like symptoms and febrile disturbances. Intermittent fevers, etc.
are also noticed.

importance. However, the patient is very chilly, easily susceptible to cold and aggravated by cold in general.

The action of this agent is very similar to that of Belladonna, except that the
sympathetic nervous system is more affected by this drug than by Belladonna. It is a
powerful narcotic and antispasmodic. The heart’s action is rendered more irregular than
by Belladonna and the involuntary muscular fibres or the bronchial tubes are relaxed to
a great extent. It produces suppressed secretions and excretions of mucous membrane.
CONSTITUTION
Just like Belladonna, Stramonium too is more or less a drug required mostly in acute
cases and as such the consideration of constitution of the patient is of little importance.
However, it is more adapted to young plethoric persons and especially children in chorea,
mania and fever with delirium.
Temperament: Bilious temperament,
Relations with heat and cold: Easily affected by cold in general.
Miasm: Psora is in the background.

PARTICULARS
Headache :
Causation: Headache is caused by shock, Sun’s heat or fright.
Location: There is intolerable pain in forehead and over the eyebrows.
Sensation: There is boring pain in forehead and tempjes. Head feels as if scattered about in many
pieces.
Modalities: Aggravation: After sleep, in darkness or looking at bright object.
Relieved: By warmth.
Concomitants: Preceded by obscure vision. Rush of blood to head. Raises the head frequently from
the pillow. Vertigo with tendency to-fall forward and to left.
Eyes:
Eyes are wide open, prominent and brilliant; pupils are widely dilated; insensible; contortion
of eyes and eyelids. Pupils dilate when child is reprimanded. Loss of vision, complains that it is dark and
calls for light. Small objects look large. All objects look black.
Face :
Face is red and hot with cold hands and feet. There is circumscribed redness on the cheeks. (Sang.).
Blood rushes to face with an expression of terror. Pale face, sometimes facial expression shows as if
smiling (Risus sardonicus). Mouth is dry, with viscid saliva; yet aversion to water. Stammering tendency.
The patient has to exert himself a long time before he can utter a word. Cannot swallow on account of
spasm of glottis; chewing motion of the mouth,
The patient vomits persistently mucus and green bile as soon as he raises head from the pillow.
Convulsion :
There is convulsion with consciousness (Nux vom.) which is very striking in this drug. Graceful
thythmic motion, convulsion especially of upper extremities and upper part of the body, There is
twitching and jerking of single muscle or a group of muscles (Acon., Agaricus, Cicuta, Zincummet,).
Chorea with violent pain in left hip. Trembling and twitching of tendons.
The convulsive attack is aggravated by dazzling and shining lights and objects.
The patient has fear of water with excessive aversion to liquids. Spasmodic contraction of throat.

name: Vertigo
author: Dubey
full:
Vertigo on opening the eyes is a strong feature of this remedy. It increases loss of consciousness
with death like pallor. Vertigo on rising or looking upward and is relieved in open fresh air and by
vomiting.
Eyes
It has a good action over the eyes.
Dim sighted—Sees as through a veil.
Amaurosis—From atrophy of retina or optic nerve, Fre-quent recurrence of amblyopia. It is also to
be thought of in stravismus when depending upon brain troubles.
Heart
It has been recommended in dilatation of the heart caused by a shock or violent physical exertion
and in angina with high tension.
Sensation : Constriction of throat and tightness feeling across the upper part of the chest.
Pain :Pain in praecordial region. Pain radiates from centre of sternum.
Pulse :Feeble, imperceptible and intermittent.
Modality : Aggravation on least motion, Indoor (in warm room) relleved in open fresh cold air,
uncovering.
Concomitant—There is paroxysmal oppression, tinnitus aurium, muscae volitantes with violent
palpitation when lying on left side and pallor of skin. Mind calm and no fear of death.
Sweat—Cold clammy sweating with coldness of body.
Gastro-intestinal tract:
Stomach :
Causation—tobacco, going at sea, during cholera.
Sensation : There is terrible, faint, sinking feeling at pit of stomach and sensation of hanging
or relaxation of stomach with incessant nausea and vomiting (Ipecac)
Nausea : With faintness; worse smell of tobacco smoke and better in open air. Vomiting with cold
sweat and worse on least motion. It is also useful in vomiting during pregnancy with much _ spitting.
Abdomen : Patient wants abdomen uncovered which relieves nausea and vorniting. Coldness in
abdomen (Colch., Lach.)
Rectum : Constipation—Chronic constipation of years standing due to inactivity of bowel or
paralysis of rectum, spasm of anal sphincter.
Diarrhoea : Sudden with nausea, vomiting, prostration, cold sweat and extreme fainting from
smell of tobacco. Stool is yellowish, greenish, slimy, watery sometimes may look like sour milk.
Urinary : Renal colic with violent spasmodic pains along left ureter accompanied by deathly nausea
and cold perspiration. (Right Ureteric Colic-Ocimum Can.)
General modalities :
Aggravation : from motion, from lying on left side, from heat, in warm room, extremes of heat and
cold,
Amelioration : Open fresh cold air, uncovering, from cold application.

full:
As far as the pathogenesis of the drug is concerned, HERING states that it has too
many characteristic actions.
On the fluids: “Dissolution of fluids of the body, which become acrid, probably caused
by Thuja which perverts lymphatic secretions; disturbs digestion and sanguinification.”
In the vegetative sphere: A surplus of life producing matter undergoes nearly
unlimited proliferation in the shape of pathological vegetations, in the shape of
me

which organise hastily. All morbid manifestations are excessive, but appear quietly so
that the beginning of the diseased state is scarcely.known. Extra unwanted growths, by
whatever name it may be called, in any and every tissue of the body, are caused by this
great “KING OF ANTI-SYCOTIC DRUGS, THUJA’”.
CONSTITUTION
Physical make-up: Hydrogenoid constitution of Grauvogl (Antim. tart., Natrum.
sulph., Medorrhinurn).Thuja is suited to patient having hydrogenoid constitution
(possessing an increased capacity to contain more and more water in the cytoplasm of the
cells; hence rain, cold, damp weather, vegetable food, etc., which increases the number of
molecules of water in the system, aggravate the symptoms). The patients are fleshy
having undue and unwanted growths, such as warts, tumours, cysts, etc., having dark
hair and dark complexion; unhealthy, oily, greasy skin, bearing warty excrescences and
dirty brownish white spots all over the body.

Blood pressure :
Veratrum viride is a very good medicine for high blood pressure whenever symptoms correspond
i.e.its peculiar pulse, characteristic tongue and face, throbbibng of carotids, BLOOD SHOT EYES AND
HEAD, etc. point to this drug.
Tonque :
The key-note of Veratrum viride is its peculiar and most characteristic tongue. The tongue is white or
yellow, but with RED STREAK DOWN THE MIDDLE. Tongue may be, dry, moist, with white or yellow
coating or no coating on either side, feels scalded (Sanquinaria) with increased saliva.
Pneumonia :
Causation: Exposure to cold or heat and sun's rays.
Mode of Onset: Sudden and violent onset.
Stage: Veratrum viride is indicated in the congestive stage or early stage and hepatisation stage of
pneumnonia.
Character: There is difficult breathing. Sensation of a heavy load on chest, Paint feeling in
STOMACH.
High fever with full hard pulse. Severe occipital headache. Livid or flushed face, cold, and clammy
perspiration. White or yellow tongue with red streak down the middle. Everything tastes sweet.
Modalities:
* Aggravation: By motion and being uncovered.
* Amelioration: By keeping quiet and lying down,
N.B. Veratrum viride will raise the opsonic index against the, Diplococcus pneumonae from 70 to
109 per cent.
Rheumatism :
Acute rheumatism with high fever; foil hartdand rapid pulse. Severe pain in joints and muscles with
scanty red urine.
Fever :
Veratrum viride may be frequently required for purerperal fever or milk fever or enteric fever or
pneumonia or suppurative fevers, or any other condition where the following symptoms are present:
Causation: Fever may come due to exposure to cold or sun's rays or extreme heat, or even after
suppression of lochia.
Mode of onset: The onset is very sudden and violent.
Character: There is unusually high rise of temperature, \.e, hyperthermia in the evening and
hypothermia in the morning,
Chill is more prominent: Patient feels cold, extremely cold with clammy perspiration. Face is flaccid

full:

Died : 30th March, 1898 Dr. Schuessler was very much influenced by Rudolph
Virchow (the founder of cellular pathology), who taught
that all diseases are based on a change in the function of
cells in the body. Another important person who influenced him greatly was Professor
Moleschott, who pointed out that the structure and vitality of the organs depends upon
the presence of inorganic constituents, Based on the theories of these two, Schuessler
formulated his own doctrine, which he called the Cell salt therapy or the Biochemic
system of medicine. He is also referred as the Father of deficiency therapy.
Dr Schuessler believed that when a human being is reduced to ashes by heat, there
are only twelve minerals left. These he called as the tissue salts. They are responsible
for the natural balance and vitality of the body, According to him, deficiency of any of
these tissue salts produces a diseased condition in the human organism, and
replenishment or supplementation of the body by the deficient salt, in physiological doses
restores health in the organism. Schuessler potentised these tissue salts and made them
into biochemic remedies.
a

Schuessler wrote a lot of books during his time. In 1873, he published his first article
on his healing system in the General homeopathic Journal, and titled it ‘An Abridged
Therapy based on physiology and cellular pathology’.
He had lot of ardent followers like Elizabeth Hubbard, Dr Stephenson, Dr. M
Blackmore and others. In 1958, Dr Blackmore popularized Schuessler’s works in his
book- ‘Colloids- A textbook for physicians’ He also refined Schuessler’s salts by adding
more tissue salts besides the existing twelve (except for sodium chloride).
The most interesting account of the application of Schuesslers’ remedies is to be
found in the book titled “Nature’s 12 Magic Healers: The Amazing Secrets of Cell Salts”
by Lionel Rolfe and Nigey Lennon, This book contains comments on the value of these
salts by two eminent homeopathic physicians, Dr. J. H. Renner MD and Dr. William E.
S. Jackson MD. Schuessler died in the year 1898, but his works have remained immortal.
HISTORY OF THE TISSUE REMEDIES
Samuel Hahnemann was the first to establish the great importance of the inorganic
cell salts as medicines of a high order thorough investigation into their pathogenetic
effects and therapeutic uses. It was his provings of Lime, Salt, Potash and Silicia that
showed what vast store-houses of medicinal force these inorganic substances are,
although wholly inert in their crude state. This prepared the way for the development of
the rest of the Tissue Remedies. He was the first who pointed out how these forces could
be unlocked and directed for therapeutic purposes,
Later, in 1832, attention was called in a paper published in Stapf's Archiv to the
great importance as remedies of all the “ essential component parts of the human body,”
and again, in the same Journal, in 1846; “All constituents of the human body principally
act on those organs wherein they have a function. All fulfill their functions when they are
the cause of symptoms.” This comes from the pen of that remarkable genius in the field
of Materia Medica — Constantine Hering.
Later on, Grauvogl, in his Text-Book, taking some notice of these remarks, amplified
them. But it remained for Dr. Schiissler, of Oldenburg, Germany, to develop these
suggestions and make the idea foreshadowed in them the basis of a “new system.” In
March, 1873, an article, entitled “ Abridged Homoeopathic Therapeutics” from his pen,
was published in a Gennan Homceopathic journal, in which he says : “About a year ago I
endeavored to discover by experiments on the sick if it were not possible to heal them,
provided their diseases were curable at all, with those substances that are the natural,
i.e., the physiological function-remedies.” Of this no special notice seems to have been
taken, until, five months subsequently, Dr. Lorbacher, of Leipzig, came out in the same
journal with some critical considerations of it. This was followed by a reply from
Schussler, which ran through seven numbers, giving a more detailed account of this
“Abridged System of Homoeopathic Therapeutics,” the important features of which are
incorporated in this work.
The original communication from Schussler to the German journal was translated
into English, and published first in the Medical Investigator, May, 1873, and soon
afterwards in a small work, by Dr. C. Hering, entitled the “ Twelve Tissue Remedies,”
}
Vv
Biochemic System of Medicine 659
“recommended for investigation” by this great teacher of our school. Several editions
were published in rapid succession, from which this historical sketch is mainly derived,
and following these appeared the translation of the twelfth German edition, by J. T.
o’Connor, M. D,, and one by M. Docetti Walker, considerably enlarged by the addition of
an appendix popularizing the Biochemic Method. Dr. Schussler, previous io his death,
which occurred early in 1898, published the 25th German edition, in which the
application of several of the remedies has been greatly enlarged and considerable new
matter added. This edition has just been translated into English.
Notwithstanding that Dr. Schussler denies in the later editions of his work all
connection with Homoeopathy, and insists that his method is not based upon the
homoeopathic law of cure, but upon physiologico-chemical processes that take place
within the organism, it is nevertheless true that the present wide adoption of the Tissue
Remedies in the treatment of disease is the fruit of the seed sown on homoepathic ground
as early as 1832, although its development was slow until Schussler gave it a wonderful
impetus by bringing physiological chemistry and physiological and pathological facts to
bear on his therapeutic procedure
THE THEORY OF SCHUSSLER’S BIOCHEMIC SYSTEM OF MEDICINE
The idea upon which Biochemic Therapeutics is based is the physiological fact that
both the structure and vitality of the organs of the body are dependent upon certain
necessary quantities and proper apportionment of its inorganic constituents. These
remain after combustion of the tissues and form the ashes.
These inorganic constituents are, in a very real sense, the material basis of the
organs and tissues of the body, and are absolutely essential to their integrity of structure
and functional activity. According to Schussler’s theory, any disturbance in the molecular
motion of these cell salts in living tissues, caused by a deficiency in the requisite amount,
constitutes disease, which can be rectified and the requisite equilibrium re-established
by administering the same mineval salts in small quantities. This is supposed to be
brought about by virtue of the operation of chemical affinity in the domain of histology ;
and hence this therapeutic procedure is styled by Schussler the Biochemie method, and
stress is laid on the fact that it is in supposed harmony with well-known facts and laws
in physiological chemistry and allied sciences.
FOUNDATION OF BIOCHEMIC SYSTEM OF MEDICINE
The foundation of Biochemistry was laid more than a century ago when Rudolph
Virchow, one of the foremost scientists of the day, discovered that the human body is
composed of an enormous number of tiny, living cells, each one made up of an
infinitesimal but perfectly balanced quantity of three classes of materials; water, organic
substances, inorganic substances.
Water and organic matter, such as sugar, albuminous and fatty substances make up the
greater portion of the body. The inorganic (mineral) elements, however, although present in
very much smaller quantities, are really vital elements; active workers which utilise the
organic substances in building the millions of cells of which the body is composed.
7 iS
660 Text Book of MATERIA MEDICA
The life of these cells is of short duration. Millions of them are constantly breaking
down and new ones are just as rapidly being built up. The necessary material for this
continuous rebuilding being supplied from the blood stream. Hence it can readily be seen
that, if the blood lacks the necessary quantities of these active, life-giving, inorganic
elements, the rebuilding process cannot proceed in a normal orderly manner, and the
resulting disturbance of the bodily rhythm gives rise to what is called “disease” in one of
its many and varied forms.
A shortage or deficiency of one or several of these vital mineral substances may arise
from a variety of causes; injuries, self-poisoning and obscure influences which in many
instances science has not yet been able to explain. The fact we have to recognise is that
“disease” - the word simply means lack of ease - indicates a disturbance of the bodily
rhythm; a disturbance which interferes with the assimilation and transport of the vital
materials essential for the repair and maintenance of living tissues. Obviously, if the
cells do not receive their proper nourishment and are not cleansed of the poisonous waste
material resulting from cellular activity, ill-health becomes inevitable.

name: The Twelve Tissue Salts
author: Dubey
full:
The twelve biochemic remedies of Schuessler, sometimes referred to as mineral salts
or tissue salts (we use the term, tissue salts), are absolutely harmless; they are not drugs
in any sense of the word. They simply provide to the system the deficient inorganic
elements, prepared homoeopathically, in an extremely finely subdivided form - a form
which ensures their ready assimilation and a speedy restoration of that balance and
harmony in the system which spell health and happiness.
There is nothing miraculous in the action of these remedies; their virtues are derived
from the application of principles based upon the laws of nature. They are to the ailing
what food is to the starving man. They bring ease by the logical process of removing the
cause of disease. The biochemic system of medicine rests upon a firm foundation; it has
stood the test of searching investigation. The more recent discoveries in the field of
biological research, and the findings of present-day biochemists, confirm its teachings. In
fact, later discoveries, made after his death, serve to pay handsome tribute to the
wonderful insight and true medical genius of Dr. W. H. Schuessler, the founder of
Biochemistry.

name: Inorganic Constituents Of Cells
author: Dubey
full:
The principal inorganic materials of nerve-cells are Mag-nesia phos., Kali phos.,
Natrum and Ferrum. Muscle-cells contain the same, with the addition of Kali mur.
Connective tissue-cells have for their specific substance Silica, while that of the
elastic tissue-cells is probably Calcarea fluor. In bone-cells we have Calcarea fluor
and Magnesia phos. and a large proportion of Calcarea phos. This latter is found in small
quantities in the cells of muscle, nerve, brain and connective tissue. Cartilage and
mucous cells have for their specific inorganic material Natrum mur., which is found
also in all solid and fluid parts of the body. Hair and the crystalline lens contain,
among other inorganic substances, also Ferrum. The carbonates, as such, are, according
to Moleschott, without any influence in the process of cell-formation

name: Frequency Of Doses
author: Dubey
full:
(a) In acute cases - a dose every hour or two
(b) In severe, painful affections - a dose every ten to fifteen minutes
(c) In chronic affections - one to four doses daily
In suitable cases the external use of the remedies is indicated and has been found
useful. For this purpose the lower triturations may be used.
In determining the dose of a biochemic remedy, the amount of the morbid product
involved is no important factor. For instance, a very small deficiency of Natrum mur. in
the cells of the epithelial layer of a serous sac may give rise to a massive serous
exudation; and as minute a supply of Natrum mur. corresponding to the deficiency may
bring about a complete resorption of the exudation.
Guided by the relative quantities of the cell salts, each practitioner can select the
proper dose of the indicated biochemic remedy.
One milligramme of a substance is estimated to contain 16 trillions of molecules.
According to this estimate, the 6th decimal trituration of it would contain about 16
billions; this quantity is more than sufficient to restore disturbed molecular motions to
the normal.
RELATION OF THE BIOCHEMIC TO THE HOMCEOPATHIC TREATMENT
Often the question has been asked, “is Schueslerism Homeopathy?” and it has as
often been answered in the affirmative as in the negative, Schuessler himself claimed
that it is not in any way related to Homoeopathy, claiming for it a separate system of
therapeutics.
i

He claims with others that the Tissue Remedies act by supplying deficiencies. This
jdea, taken literally, seems erroneous; for example, in a disturbance of the molecules of
Natr. mur. there is not necessarily a deficiency in the amount Natr. mur. in the body, but
rather a lack of continuity in the arrangement of the existing molecules in the body. This
salt given as a remedy does not supply a lack or deficiency of salt, as the quantity given

where it may be needed. It uses albumen as a cement to build up bone structure. Thus it
gives solidity to the bones.
Bone is fifty-seven per cent, phosphate of lime, the remainder gelatine; an
albuminous, gluey substance, carbonate of soda, magnesium phosphate and sodium
chloride. Without the lime phosphate no bone can be made. It is the nutritive salt for the
periostium and through it for bones.
Calcarea phos also supplies new blood cells, thus becoming the first remedy in
anemia. Without Cale Phos there could be no blood coagulation.

frequently the cause of indigestion.

prevent an acid condition from prevailing, and under certain conditions, when calcium
phosphate for any reason is not present in proper quantities, the affinities draw upon
sodium phosphate in an endeavor to supply the lack, and thus a deficiency in the alkaline

author: Dubey
full:
1. This tissue salt is concerned with the formation of bone and teeth and thus becomes
an important remedy for children. It aids growth and normal development and
should be given in cases of backwardness more particularly where there is bone
weakness or recurring tooth troubles.
2. Tardy formation of callus around the ends of fractured bones, in the unnatural
growth and defective nutrition of bone and other textures found in rickets and
similar diseased conditions; thus the sphere of action of this remedy includes al!
bone diseases.
3. Defective nutrition, imperfect cell-growth and consequent decay and destruction of
tissue, especially the osseous and glandular systems. It is of use during dentition,
in convulsions and spasms occurring in weak, scrofulous subjects, stimulating
nutrition, etc.
4. It promotes healthy cellular activity and restores tone to weakened organs and
tissues. This is the remedy for any period of convalescence; its restorative power
will speed recovery and replenish the body’s reserves of strength. Calc Phos has
always been prized as a restorative.
Another important feature is its restorative power after acute diseases, either
directly or preparing the way for other remedies, by stimulating the system to their
action, thus becoming an important intercurent remedy.
Practically, this drug proves itself a real tonic in chronic wasting diseases. In
anemia of young, rapidly growing people; in women weakened by rapid child-
bearing, prolonged suckling or excessive menstruation or leucorrhea; in
accompanying diseases with exhaustive discharges, as in chronic bronchitis,
tubercular diarrhea and night-sweats, abscesses and scrofulous sores, through its
great power on the secretions, it acts curatively.
5. It is a constituent of saliva and gastric juice. It assists digestion and assimilation
and favours the building up of a sturdy, robust constitution.
6. In old age, where the regenerative function decreases in the nervous tissue, Cale.
phos. is well indicated, and we find it useful in senile cutaneous and vaginal itching,
as well as during reconvalescence from severe acute diseases. In tuberculosis
pulmonum, with its emaciation, night-sweats, hemoptysis and other marked
physical symptoms, Cale. phos. in low potencies holds out great promise to
ameliorate the severity of the case; equally great is its benefit in pollutions of young
married men (and sexual excitement of women) and onanists. In the osseous
expansions of rachitic children.
7. Cale Phos is the tissue salt for anemia and conditions associated with imperfect
circulation. In the anaemic states often seen in young girls, this remedy should be
given. 10 grains of the second trituration of Cal.phos. is preferable to the usual iron
treatment.

1. Fever : A deficiency of this cell salt is the cause of fevers and inflammatory
conditions and so indicated in all febrile disturbances and in inflammatory and
congestive diseases at the beginning, especially before exudation has commenced.
The principal accompaniments of these conditions calling for Ferrum Phos are
manifested by flushed face, fever with full pulse, hot, dry skin, thirst, pain and
redness of the part. It should be administered at frequent intervals until the
inflammatory symptoms subside.
Useful in the first stage of enteric, gastric, typhoid, typhus, rheumatic and scarlet
fever, measles,chicken-pox,small-pox, etc., for the heat and congestion. Intermittent
fever, with vomiting of food; catarrhal fever, with quickened pulse and chilly
sensations.
2. Respiratory Organs : All inflammatory conditions of the respiratory tract, in the
first stage, for the fever, heat and pain. Pneumonia, bronchitis, pleuritis, tracheitis,
etc., in the inflammatory stage, and, indeed, as long as the pain lasts. It is followed
well by Kali mur. in the second stage or that of expectoration of white mucus.

blood. Soreness of the chest. Breathing short and hurried at the beginning or during
the course of the disease, when there is heat and fever present. Cold in the chest,
with hard, dry cough and soreness in the lungs (Kali mur.’). Acute, painful, short,
irritating cough. In the beginning of all coughs and colds this is the first remedy.

the chest. Painful hoarseness and huskiness of speakers and singers, when due to
the irritation of the bronchii (Calc. phos.). Congestion of the lungs, acute or chronic,
with oppression and pain; catch in breath, pleurisy, pain in the side, in first stage.

wounds, cuts and abrasions can be controlled with a little powdered Ferr Phos,
applied directly to the injured parts. A few tablets may be crushed for this purpose

blood corpuscles, as in anaemia.

blood, and probably in intercellular fluids: and that all such conditions arise from the
inability of the digestion and assimilation to furnish sufficient quantity of sodium
sulphate to carry off the excess of water breathed into the blood through the lungs.
When the blood becomes overcharged with water, of course, the various tissues of the
body must suffer from lack of proper nourishment. This sets up a panic. Now, as the

blood with water.

basements, etc., or from eating water-plants, fish, etc. Symptoms aggravated by the
use of water in any form. Conditions which tend to increase the water in the system,
such as living in low, marshy places, “ague districts “ will cause a. molecular
disturbance of Natr. sulph.

author: Dubey
full:
1. It is especially suited to imperfectly nourished constitutions, owing to deficient
assimilation and corresponds to the scrofulous diathesis.
2. Silica “For Lack of Grit — Physical or mental”. Silica provides the “grit” of most
living things. It is indicated by those who need more stamina, especially when
malnutrition is present. Lack of stamina — mental, physical. Weakened and
exhausted states — exhausted after a few hours, to regain energy after surgery.
Lack of self-confidence coming from sense of weakness and lack of courage.
3. Sensitive to cold. Wants to wrap up warm. Lack of body warmth — desire warmth, <
cold and cold wind
4. The characteristic discharge of silicea is thick, yellow, and offensive. It is the
biochemic remedy for offensive discharges.
5. Excessive offensive perspiration of feet, arm pits and back of neck. Offensive foot
sweat with cold feet. Diseases resulting from suppression of foot-sweat, for instance:
amblyopia, cataract, paralyses, etc.
6. Milk intolerant, even of mother’s milk
7, Silica is indicated wherever there is pus formation or threatened suppuration, e.g.
abscesses, boils, gumboils, styes, etc. It is useful in the treatment of tonsillitis when
pus has begun to form.
8. Skin
* It is the remedy for ailments attended with pus-formation, and is closely related
to all fistulous burrowings. Wherever pus is formed in an inflamed part of
connective tissue or skin, Silicea may be used.
Like Cal. sulph, Silicea corresponds to the process of suppuration, with the
following distinguishing features: Silicea ripens abscess, since it promotes
suppuration. Calc. sulph, by restraining the suppurative process, heals
suppurating wounds. As long as infiltration, which can only disappear by
suppuration, lasts, Silicea is the remedy, and should be continued until all the
infiltrated parts have disappeared. If then the wound fails to heal, give Calc.
sulph.
